detail.body: ### What does this PR do? Depends on: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51368 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52552 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52626 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53361 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56327 - https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6044 - https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6199 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7054 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7521 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7522 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8018 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7763 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7762 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7500 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7501 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7502 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7503 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7678 Adds DeepSeek V4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM5.3 Flash LoRA support to verl's vLLM weight-sync path. Previously a merge=False LoRA base sync orphaned the `.base_layer.` suffix on wrapped modules and mishandled the mxfp4 quant path, so DSV4 LoRA diverged from the actor. This reworks weight-name reconciliation to be runtime-probed (strict vs flat loader) instead of model-type-based, unwraps the LoRA-installed mxfp4 quant-method wrapper, and threads `peft_config` through the FP8/mxfp4 load path so the same reconciliation applies there. Tested with Megatron backend, GPU E2E (DSV4 merge=F GRPO, 2-node): step1/step2 pearson 0.9970/0.9950, aligned to run15 merge=T 0.9952/0.9944. ### Checklist Before Starting - [X] Search for similar PRs. Query: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=deepseek+v4+lora - [X] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI) - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off` - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]` - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test` - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title. - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching` ### Test ```bash pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py # GPU E2E: DSV4 merge=F GRPO 2-node — step1/step2 pearson 0.9970/0.9950 vs run15 merge=T 0.9952/0.9944 ``` Unit tests cover strict-vs-flat loader detection, per-expert routed leaves, and non-LoRA params on wrapped modules (e.g. DSV4 `gate.tid2eid` / `gate.e_score_correction_bias`). ### API and Usage Example For GLM-5.3-Flash, prepare every Ray node with a Bridge build providing `GLM53FlashModel` and its paired Megatron-Core, then launch with `VERL_USE_UV=0`. The frozen `megatron` extra pins Bridge 0.6.2, which lacks this wrapper. DSW CPU import checks passed against both the documented upstream source pair (Bridge `58382ddf`, Core `902feb8e`) and the separate Bridge `d16c26d5` environment used for GLM training. [Per-node setup and import check](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/cd9330c25a9408aeedc87a5abfb88562e9318a05/examples/tuning/lora/run_glm53_flash_megatron.sh#L12-L19) No CLI/API change. Behavior is automatic: `resolve_weight_name` probes the inner model's `load_weights` at runtime and toggles `.base_layer.` accordingly. For DSV4 merge=False LoRA, no extra config is needed beyond enabling LoRA + `merge=False`. ```bash # DSV4 merge=False LoRA (existing config; no new flags) actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.enable=True actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=False actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.target_modules='["linear_wkv","linear_wgate","linear_wq_b","linear_weights_proj","linear_kv_proj","linear_q_down_proj","linear_q_up_proj","linear_proj","linear_fc1","linear_fc2","router"]' ``` ### Design & Code Changes **Runtime-probed `.base_layer.` reconciliation** (`verl/utils/vllm/utils.py`) - Adds `_inner_load_weights_is_strict`: probes the inner transformer's `load_weights` bytecode (`co_names`) to decide strict (keeps `.base_layer.`, DeepseekV2/DSV4) vs flat (strips it, Llama/Qwen3.5). Cached per class. - `resolve_weight_name` toggles one `.base_layer.` segment loader-style-aware, re-adds the suffix for non-LoRA params on a wrapped module, and reconciles per-expert routed leaves (strict keep / flat strip, gated by `_HAS_LORA_BASE_LAYER_PREFIX`). **mxfp4 LoRA unwrap** (`verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp4_utils.py`) - Adds `_resolve_mxfp4_quant_method`: unwraps the `FusedMoEModularMethod` wrapper that merge=False LoRA installs over `Mxfp4MoEMethod` (stored as `old_quant_method`) so staging, layout derivation, and `process_weights_after_loading` repack reach the legacy method — the modular wrapper inherits a no-op post-load and would otherwise skip the repack. **FP8/mxfp4 name reconciliation** (`verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py`) - `load_quanted_weights` gains a `peft_config` parameter; when set (LoRA base sync), names run through `resolve_weight_name` against live params/buffers so `.base_layer.` is reconciled on the FP8/mxfp4 path too (e.g. DSV4 `compressor.fused_wkv_wgate`). Callers thread `peft_config` for both base and drafter loads. **LoRA MoE prefix** (`verl/utils/vllm/patch.py`) - Removes the eager `lora_base_layer_prefix` clearing block; the prefix is now reconciled through `resolve_weight_name` instead. **Tests** (`tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py`) - Expanded coverage for strict-vs-flat loader detection, per-expert routed leaves, and non-LoRA params on wrapped modules. ### Checklist Before Submitting > [!IMPORTANT] > Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review. - [X] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [X] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` - [X] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). - [X] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: ... - [X] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).) - [X] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`. ✨ Presented to you with [Mind Lab](https://www.mindlab.im/) - A Lab for Experiential Intelligence. ### Review follow-up validation The follow-ups on this existing feature PR address its review findings, rather than proposing a duplicate PR. Changes cover strict-loader scope, FP8 refit hooks, quantization overrides, and multimodal/router replay alignment. AI assistance was used for these follow-up fixes and review checks. DSW validation used an isolated source checkout. The following suites passed 381 tests in total with no skips. Real two-process Gloo CP=2 and native vLLM server probes also passed. All pre-commit hooks passed, as did syntax checks for the three launchers and a stubbed GLM launcher argument check. ```bash python -m pytest -q -rs \ tests/utils/test_model_on_cpu.py \ tests/workers/engine/megatron/test_router_replay_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_megatron_router_replay_dcp.py \ tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_rollout_quantization_overrides_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_fp8_restage_same_shape_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py \ tests/workers/rollout/test_routing_replay_prompt_alignment_on_cpu.py # 188 passed python -m pytest -q -rs tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_agent_loop_tq_on_cpu.py # 8 passed python -m pytest -q -rs tests/utils/test_continuous_token_on_cpu.py tests/models/test_model_forward_fused.py tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_mtp_hybrid_sleep_acceptance_on_cpu.py # 185 passed ```

detail.title: [vllm] feat: Support LoRA for DeepSeek V4 & DeepSeek V4.1 & GLM5.3 Flash

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,345 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -xeuo pipefail
+
+# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash VLM BF16 LoRA merge=False — Geo3K alignment test.
+
+export CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
+export NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
+export TORCH_NCCL_AVOID_RECORD_STREAMS=1
+export VLLM_USE_V1=1
+export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
+export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
+export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True"
+
+project_name='DAPO'
+exp_name=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-'DAPO-deepseek-v41-flash-megatron-lora-vl-geo3k'}
+
+adv_estimator=grpo
+gamma=1.0
+
+use_kl_in_reward=False
+kl_coef=0.0
+use_kl_loss=False
+kl_loss_coef=0.0
+
+clip_ratio_low=0.2
+clip_ratio_high=0.28
+
+max_prompt_length=${MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH:-2048}
+max_response_length=${MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH:-16384}
+enable_overlong_buffer=False
+overlong_buffer_len=${max_response_length}
+overlong_penalty_factor=1.0
+
+loss_agg_mode="token-mean"
+
+# Keep the trajectory batch divisible by the training data-parallel size and
+# by ppo_mini_batch_size * rollout.n.
+train_prompt_bsz=${TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE:-64}
+n_resp_per_prompt=${ROLLOUT_N:-8}
+train_prompt_mini_bsz=${PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE:-64}
+
+rollout_is="token"
+rollout_is_threshold="0.5_5.0"
+rollout_is_batch_normalize="true"
+
+bypass_mode="false"
+loss_type="ppo_clip"
+
+ROUTING_REPLAY_MODE="R3"
+
+NNODES=${NNODES:-4}
+RAY_DATA_HOME=${RAY_DATA_HOME:-"${HOME}/verl"}
+MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-"${RAY_DATA_HOME}/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash"}
+CKPTS_DIR=${CKPTS_DIR:-"${RAY_DATA_HOME}/ckpts/${project_name}/${exp_name}"}
+TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-"${RAY_DATA_HOME}/data/geo3k/train.parquet"}
+TEST_FILE=${TEST_FILE:-"${RAY_DATA_HOME}/data/geo3k/test.parquet"}
+
+temperature=1.0
+top_p=1.0
+top_k=-1 # 0 for HF rollout, -1 for vLLM rollout
+
+use_dynamic_bsz=True
+actor_ppo_max_token_len=${PPO_MAX_TOKEN_LEN_PER_GPU:-12288}
+infer_ppo_max_token_len=${actor_ppo_max_token_len}
+gen_tp=${ROLLOUT_TP:-8}
+gen_ep=${gen_tp}
+gen_pp=1
+gen_dcp=1
+train_tp=1
+train_pp=1
+train_cp=${TRAIN_CP:-${ACTOR_CP:-4}}
+train_ep=${TRAIN_EP:-$((NNODES * 8))}
+train_etp=1
+
+RECOMPUTE_GRANULARITY=${RECOMPUTE_GRANULARITY:-full}
+RECOMPUTE_METHOD=${RECOMPUTE_METHOD:-uniform}
+RECOMPUTE_NUM_LAYERS=${RECOMPUTE_NUM_LAYERS:-1}
+
+use_remove_padding=True
+RECOMPUTE_ARGS=(
+    ++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.recompute_method=${RECOMPUTE_METHOD}
+    ++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.recompute_granularity=${RECOMPUTE_GRANULARITY}
+    ++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.recompute_num_layers=${RECOMPUTE_NUM_LAYERS}
+)
+lora_rank=16
+lora_alpha=32
+lora_plus_ratio=${LORA_PLUS_RATIO:-1.0}
+actor_lr=${ACTOR_LR:-5e-5}
+
+# ``last20_all_vision`` is the default training scope: the last 20 of 40 HF
+# decoder blocks (native layers 40..79), plus vision tower and aligner LoRA.
+# ``first20_all_vision`` selects the first 20 HF blocks (native layers 0..39)
+# with the same vision tower and aligner LoRA path. The native model
+# interleaves attention (even layers) and MoE (odd layers), so generate only
+# module patterns that can actually exist at each layer.
+lora_scope=${LORA_SCOPE:-last20_all_vision}
+lora_target_modules='["linear_wkv","linear_wgate","linear_kv_proj","linear_q_down_proj","linear_q_up_proj","linear_o_group_proj","linear_proj","linear_fc1","linear_fc2","vision.patch_embed.proj","vision.blocks.*.attn.wqkv","vision.blocks.*.attn.wo","vision.blocks.*.mlp.w1","vision.blocks.*.mlp.w2","aligner.w1","aligner.w2"]'
+if [[ "${lora_scope}" == "first20_all_vision" || "${lora_scope}" == "last20_all_vision" || "${lora_scope}" == "first20_novision" || "${lora_scope}" == "last20_novision" ]]; then
+    _with_vision=1
+    [[ "${lora_scope}" == *novision ]] && _with_vision=0
+    decoder_hf_total_layers=40
+    decoder_hf_lora_layer_count=20
+    if [[ "${lora_scope}" == first20* ]]; then
+        decoder_native_start_layer=0
+        decoder_native_end_layer=$((2 * decoder_hf_lora_layer_count))
+    else
+        decoder_native_start_layer=$((2 * (decoder_hf_total_layers - decoder_hf_lora_layer_count)))
+        decoder_native_end_layer=$((2 * decoder_hf_total_layers))
+    fi
+    decoder_native_total_layers=$((2 * decoder_hf_total_layers))
+    if ((decoder_native_start_layer < 0)); then
+        echo "Invalid DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder layer range" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+
+    lora_target_modules="["
+    first_target=1
+    for ((layer=decoder_native_start_layer; layer<decoder_native_end_layer; layer++)); do
+        if ((layer % 2 == 0)); then
+            # CSA2 keeps the compressor only on KV-source layers and the
+            # indexer only on index-source layers; list only modules that
+            # exist to avoid unmatched-target warnings.
+            layer_modules=(linear_kv_proj linear_q_down_proj linear_q_up_proj linear_o_group_proj linear_proj)
+            if ((layer == 4 || layer == 16 || layer == 28 || layer == 40)); then
+                layer_modules+=(linear_wkv linear_wgate)
+            fi
+            if [[ "${lora_scope}" == last20* ]] && ((layer == 40)); then
+                layer_modules=(linear_q_down_proj linear_q_up_proj linear_o_group_proj linear_proj)
+            fi
+        else
+            layer_modules=(linear_fc1 linear_fc2)
+        fi
+        for module in "${layer_modules[@]}"; do
+            if ((first_target == 0)); then lora_target_modules+=","; fi
+            lora_target_modules+="\"*.layers.${layer}.*.${module}\""
+            first_target=0
+        done
+    done
+    if ((_with_vision == 1)); then
+        lora_target_modules+=',"vision.patch_embed.proj","vision.blocks.*.attn.wqkv","vision.blocks.*.attn.wo","vision.blocks.*.mlp.w1","vision.blocks.*.mlp.w2"'
+        lora_target_modules+=',"aligner.w1","aligner.w2"]'
+    else
+        lora_target_modules+=']'
+    fi
+    unset _with_vision
+elif [[ "${lora_scope}" != "all" ]]; then
+    echo "Unsupported LORA_SCOPE=${lora_scope}; use all, first20_all_vision, last20_all_vision, first20_novision, or last20_novision" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+# Adapter-only post-processing is fixed in the current Verl path.  Keeping the
+# base resident avoids reloading the full model on every update and preserves
+# the tested low-overhead sleep-level-1 path.
+ROLLOUT_RESYNC_BASE=${ROLLOUT_RESYNC_BASE:-False}
+ROLLOUT_GPU_MEM_UTIL=${ROLLOUT_GPU_MEM_UTIL:-0.30}
+ROLLOUT_MAX_MODEL_LEN=${ROLLOUT_MAX_MODEL_LEN:-32768}
+ROLLOUT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS=${ROLLOUT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS:-4096}
+ROLLOUT_MAX_NUM_SEQS=${ROLLOUT_MAX_NUM_SEQS:-8}
+VLLM_MOE_BACKEND=${VLLM_MOE_BACKEND:-auto}
+VLLM_LINEAR_BACKEND=${VLLM_LINEAR_BACKEND:-auto}
+TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=${TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS:-400}
+TOTAL_EPOCHS=${TOTAL_EPOCHS:-13}
+SAVE_FREQ=${SAVE_FREQ:--1}
+PARAM_OFFLOAD=${PARAM_OFFLOAD:-False}
+OPTIMIZER_OFFLOAD=${OPTIMIZER_OFFLOAD:-False}
+OPTIMIZER_OFFLOAD_FRACTION=${OPTIMIZER_OFFLOAD_FRACTION:-1.0}
+LR_WARMUP_STEPS=${LR_WARMUP_STEPS:-3}
+ENGRAM_CPU_LOOKUP=${ENGRAM_CPU_LOOKUP:-True}
+
+if ((gen_tp < 1 || 24 % gen_tp != 0 || train_ep % gen_tp != 0)); then
+    echo "DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram requires gen_tp to be positive and divide 24, and train_ep to be divisible by gen_tp (got gen_tp=${gen_tp}, train_ep=${train_ep})." >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+train_data_bsz=$((train_prompt_bsz * n_resp_per_prompt))
+if ((train_data_bsz % (train_prompt_mini_bsz * n_resp_per_prompt) != 0)); then
+    echo "Trajectory batch ${train_data_bsz} is not divisible by mini*n=${train_prompt_mini_bsz}*${n_resp_per_prompt}" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+run() {
+    if [ "${DRY_RUN:-0}" = 1 ]; then
+        printf '%q ' "$@"
+        printf '\n'
+    else
+        "$@"
+    fi
+}
+
+run python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
+    model_engine=megatron \
+    +ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars.PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="${PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF}" \
+    data.train_files="${TRAIN_FILE}" \
+    data.val_files="${TEST_FILE}" \
+    data.prompt_key=prompt \
+    data.image_key=images \
+    data.trust_remote_code=True \
+    data.return_raw_chat=True \
+    +data.apply_chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=${ENABLE_THINKING:-True} \
+    data.filter_overlong_prompts=${FILTER_OVERLONG_PROMPTS:-False} \
+    +data.apply_chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort=${REASONING_EFFORT:-max} \
+    data.truncation=left \
+    data.max_prompt_length=${max_prompt_length} \
+    data.max_response_length=${max_response_length} \
+    data.train_batch_size=${train_prompt_bsz} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=${n_resp_per_prompt} \
+    algorithm.adv_estimator=${adv_estimator} \
+    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=${use_kl_in_reward} \
+    algorithm.kl_ctrl.kl_coef=${kl_coef} \
+    algorithm.gamma=${gamma} \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is=${rollout_is} \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is_threshold=${rollout_is_threshold} \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is_batch_normalize=${rollout_is_batch_normalize} \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode=${bypass_mode} \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.loss_type=${loss_type} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=${use_kl_loss} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=${kl_loss_coef} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=${clip_ratio_low} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=${clip_ratio_high} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_c=10.0 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.experts_shared_outer_loras=True \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.lora_plus_ratio=${lora_plus_ratio} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${MODEL_PATH}" \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.trust_remote_code=True \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=False \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.mtp.enable=False \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
+    +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.num_nextn_predict_layers=0 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.rank=${lora_rank} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.alpha=${lora_alpha} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.lora_A_init_method=kaiming \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=False \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.resync_base=${ROLLOUT_RESYNC_BASE} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.dtype=bf16 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.target_modules="${lora_target_modules}" \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.enable_tower_connector_lora=${ENABLE_TOWER_CONNECTOR_LORA:-True} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=${use_remove_padding} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_remove_padding=${use_remove_padding} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.use_remove_padding=${use_remove_padding} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=${actor_lr} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_warmup_steps=${LR_WARMUP_STEPS} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.weight_decay=0 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=${train_prompt_mini_bsz} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_mbridge=True \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.sequence_parallel=False \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_megatron_fsdp=False \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_offload=${PARAM_OFFLOAD} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimizer_offload=${OPTIMIZER_OFFLOAD} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size=${train_pp} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size=${train_tp} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.expert_model_parallel_size=${train_ep} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.expert_tensor_parallel_size=${train_etp} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.context_parallel_size=${train_cp} \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.clip_grad=1.0 \
+    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=${loss_agg_mode} \

+def _multimodal_fp8():
+    """A multimodal checkpoint whose FP8 config lives on the text config only."""
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        model_type="vl", quantization_config=None, text_config=SimpleNamespace(quantization_config=_FP8)
+    )

+def _rollout(hf_overrides=None, name="vllm"):
+    engine_kwargs = {} if hf_overrides is None else {"vllm": {"hf_overrides": hf_overrides}}

+        name=name,

+        # A nested null clears the text-level config: vLLM then serves an unquantized rollout.
+        ({"text_config": {"quantization_config": None}}, (True, None)),
+        # A top-level null leaves vLLM's fallback to the text-level config in place.
+        ({"quantization_config": None}, (True, _FP8)),
+        ({"quantization_config": None, "text_config": {"quantization_config": None}}, (True, None)),
+        # A nested mapping merges into the checkpoint's config key by key.
+        (
+            {"text_config": {"quantization_config": {"activation_scheme": "static"}}},
+            (True, {**_FP8, "activation_scheme": "static"}),
+        ),
+        # A top-level config wins over the text-level one.
+        ({"quantization_config": _CT, "text_config": {"quantization_config": None}}, (True, _CT)),
+        # Other text_config overrides leave the quantization alone.
+        ({"text_config": {"rope_theta": 1.0}}, (False, _FP8)),

+def expand_image_tokens(input_ids, image_grid_hws, image_token_id, downsample_ratio):
+    """Expand [sequence] image placeholders, returning [1, sequence] IDs and types."""
+    raw_ids = input_ids.reshape(-1).tolist()
+    grids = image_grid_hws.tolist()
+    if raw_ids.count(image_token_id) != len(grids):
+        raise ValueError("DeepSeek-V4.1 requires one unexpanded placeholder per image")
+    grids = iter(grids)
+    ids, types = [], []
+    for token in raw_ids:
+        if token != image_token_id:
+            ids.append(token)
+            types.append(-1)
+            continue
+        height, width = next(grids)
+        height = (height + downsample_ratio - 1) // downsample_ratio
+        width = (width + downsample_ratio - 1) // downsample_ratio
+        span = [0] + ([1] * width + [2]) * height + [3]
+        ids.extend([image_token_id] * len(span))
+        types.extend(span)
+    return input_ids.new_tensor([ids]), input_ids.new_tensor([types])
+

**Check span-scanner termination against the `expand_image_tokens` type layout.**

`expand_image_tokens` emits each span as `0, (1*w, 2)*h, 3`. The scanner moves past `0`. While the next token is `1` (IMAGE), it consumes the run of `1` values and then one extra token (`2`). ## `dp_balanced` in Megatron Core `core_v0.19.2`

`max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` is the **per-rank token budget** for each packed microbatch. The scheduler uses a total pack limit of:

\[
\text{pack limit} = \texttt{max\_seqlen\_per\_dp\_cp\_rank} \times \texttt{context\_parallel\_size}
\]

So, for example, a per-rank limit of 8,192 with CP=4 allows up to 32,768 tokens in a pack. The configuration requires this value when `sequence_packing_scheduler` is set; `dp_balanced` is the supported scheduler named in the config. ([github.com](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/megatron/core/model_parallel_config.py?utm_source=openai))

At a high level, the path gathers sequence lengths across DP ranks, schedules samples into packs under that limit, then builds packed THD microbatches with sequence-boundary metadata. It can balance packed work across DP ranks, and the number of scheduled microbatches can vary by step. ([docs.nvidia.com](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/megatron-bridge/nightly/training/packed-sequences.html?utm_source=openai))

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Restore the package after the quantized tests.** When pytest collects this file, `_load_vllm_quant_utils()` replaces `verl.utils.vllm` in `sys.modules` and leaves the stub installed. Scope all three module substitutions to the tests that need them, and restore their previous values afterward. Python uses `sys.modules` to cache loaded modules. **Resolve the nested quantization configuration before treating a null override as BF16.** When `text_config.quantization_config` is set, vLLM 0.32.0 applies `hf_overrides` to the top-level config, then falls back to `text_config.quantization_config` when the top-level value is `None`. The rollout therefore remains quantized, while this dispatcher returns no quantizer and exports BF16 weights.

**Precompute the live-name suffix lookup.** `live_weight_dtype` calls `match_dtype` for each `weight`, `weight_scale`, and `weight_scale_inv` leaf. Each call can perform up to four full scans: two name candidates and up to two mapped candidates. Routed expert leaves can miss because the live model exposes fused expert parameters, not per-expert parameter names. A DSV4-sized model has 43 layers and 256 routed experts. The exact Python time depends on the concrete vLLM parameter namespace and update contents, so a seconds-scale or billion-comparison figure is not established here. However, the repeated scans are not negligible at this model scale and are unnecessary. Build a suffix-to-dtype lookup once before the weight loop. This preserves the current exact-or-dotted-suffix matching and unique-dtype behavior.

### Chat

There are 3 ways to chat with [CodeRabbit](https://coderabbit.ai?utm_source=oss&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=verl-project/verl&utm_content=7483):

- Review comments: Directly reply to a review comment made by CodeRabbit. Example:
  - `I pushed a fix in commit <commit_id>, please review it.`
  - `Open a follow-up GitHub issue for this discussion.`
- Files and specific lines of code (under the "Files changed" tab): Tag `@coderabbitai` in a new review comment at the desired location with your query.
- PR comments: Tag `@coderabbitai` in a new PR comment to ask questions about the PR branch. For the best results, please provide a very specific query, as very limited context is provided in this mode. Examples:
  - `@coderabbitai gather interesting stats about this repository and render them as a table. Additionally, render a pie chart showing the language distribution in the codebase.`
  - `@coderabbitai read the files in the src/scheduler package and generate a class diagram using mermaid and a README in the markdown format.`

### CodeRabbit commands

> These commands are invoked using PR/Issue comments.

- `@coderabbitai pause` to pause the reviews on a PR.
- `@coderabbitai resume` to resume the paused reviews.
- `@coderabbitai review` to trigger an incremental review. This is useful when automatic reviews are disabled for the repository.
- `@coderabbitai full review` to do a full review from scratch and review all the files again.
- `@coderabbitai review --preview-config` to test the unmerged CodeRabbit configuration on a draft PR. The requester must have repository write access; preview results are non-authoritative.
- `@coderabbitai rate limit` to show your current review rate limit status.
- `@coderabbitai summary` to regenerate the summary of the PR.
- `@coderabbitai track` in a human-authored review thread to track the original finding until CodeRabbit verifies it is fixed.
- `@coderabbitai fixed` in a tracked review thread to verify the current code against the original finding.
- `@coderabbitai evaluate custom pre-merge check --instructions <custom-checks-instructions> --name <custom-checks-title> [--mode <error|warning>]` to validate the custom pre-merge checks instructions. Defaults to `error` when `--mode` is omitted.
- `@coderabbitai ignore pre-merge checks` to override pre-merge checks and get an approval on PR.
- `@coderabbitai run pre-merge checks` to run pre-merge checks on the pull request.
- `@coderabbitai generate sequence diagram` to generate a sequence diagram of the changes in this PR.
- `@coderabbitai emit path instructions` to emit generated path-specific review instructions for this repository.
- `@coderabbitai generate project vocabulary` to list vocabulary that is specific to this repository.
- `@coderabbitai resolve merge conflict` to automatically resolve merge conflicts.
- `@coderabbitai autofix` to automatically fix issues in the current review thread, or all unresolved review comments when used in the PR conversation.
- `@coderabbitai autopilot` to enable Autofix to fix CodeRabbit findings and required CI, and resolve merge conflicts.
- `@coderabbitai autopilot resume` to resume Autofix for this PR.
- `@coderabbitai autopilot stop` to stop Autofix for this PR.
- `@coderabbitai fix-ci` to automatically fix failing CI checks in a stacked pull request.
- `@coderabbitai fix-ci commit` to automatically fix failing CI checks by committing fixes to the current branch.
- `@coderabbitai resolve` to resolve all the CodeRabbit review comments.
- `@coderabbitai configuration` to show the current CodeRabbit configuration for the repository.
- `@coderabbitai generate configuration` to create a PR that adds the current resolved configuration as `.coderabbit.yaml` (or show it if already present).
- `@coderabbitai help` to get help.

### Other keywords and placeholders

- Add `@coderabbitai ignore` or `@coderabbit ignore` anywhere in the PR description to prevent this PR from being reviewed.
- Add `@coderabbitai summary` to generate the high-level summary at a specific location in the PR description.
- Add `@coderabbitai` anywhere in the PR title to generate the title automatically.

### CodeRabbit configuration file (`.coderabbit.yaml`)

- You can programmatically configure CodeRabbit by adding a `.coderabbit.yaml` file to the root of your repository.
- Please see the [configuration documentation](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/configure-coderabbit) for more information.
- You can also validate your configuration using the [online YAML validator](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration/yaml-validator).
- If your editor has YAML language server enabled, you can add the path at the top of this file to enable auto-completion and validation: `# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json`


### Status, support, documentation and community

- Visit our [status page](https://status.coderabbit.ai) to check the current availability of CodeRabbit.

- Visit our [documentation site](https://docs.coderabbit.ai) for detailed information on how to use CodeRabbit.

# Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).

issue_comments.body:
Rechecked all inline findings and the actionable items embedded in earlier review summaries against the current source. The merge-risk text still refers to `caa67661`; the subsequent fixes are now pushed.

The functional fixes are in [14d666d1](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/commit/14d666d1b8a1aa467811aebca4a92bfbdb38a97c). The fused-forward test configuration and remaining launcher follow-ups are also pushed. Every new commit is GPG-signed and has only the author's Signed-off-by trailer.

Outside-diff and general-review findings have the following outcomes.

- [5489854872](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5489854872) and [5525114601](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5525114601): removed the redundant GLM DATA-array continuation in [ad086ea8](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/commit/ad086ea80e116cddf7e476839a3ba3267a091129). The DeepSeek V4 launcher retains its original root/path configuration; no new environment-variable validation was added. Both launcher syntax checks and a stubbed GLM argument check passed.
- [5504901796](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5504901796): already addressed. The merged hf_overrides is written after the engine_kwargs expansion, so it is not replaced by the original input.
- [5576399141](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5576399141) and [5577810069](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5577810069): fixed the inherited no-op FP8 LoRA hook, shared hf_overrides validation, and exact strict-loader subtree scope. Tests cover old and delegating wrappers, live storage, mapped VLM prefixes, sibling lm_head weights, and genuinely strict roots.
- [5645089780](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5645089780) and [5645305674](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5645305674): already addressed. The multimodal SFT path rejects truncation that would break image alignment and emits vision_token_types only with the matching image tensors.
- [5657608990](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5657608990), [5686797119](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5686797119), and [5709398773](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5709398773): the obsolete engine-stub test was removed. The replacement suite calls the real prompt-comparison helper. It distinguishes V4.1 compact expansion from other models and rejects mismatched already-expanded spans, including equal-total-length shifts and missing adjacent images.
- [5725286496](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5725286496): already addressed. Unsupported HybridModel builds decline fused patching and the engine falls back to unfused forward. The backend-selection and wrapper-chain tests pass on the DSW Megatron installation.
- [5728820172](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5728820172): no tuple-unpacking change is needed for the supported full-stream GLM53 wrapper. The fused call supplies labels but no loss_mask. The inspected Bridge wrapper returns the hook output directly in that case; its tuple return requires a non-None loss_mask and reordering. This conclusion is specific to that wrapper contract.
- [5729715221](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5729715221): batch order is preserved with explicit text rows. Scale dropping is restricted to unquantized BF16/FP16/FP32 targets; the int8 scale regression passes.
- [5729850348](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5729850348): fixed omitted modality rows using each sample's effective input length. A supplied but short row still raises instead of hiding malformed metadata.
- [5735611037](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5735611037): already addressed. DeepSeek V4/V4.1 dispatch rejects changed or cleared native quantization layouts before the unquantized-export return.
- [5758344253](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5758344253): fixed BSHD R2 static-CP recording. uint8 CP shards are gathered and restored in zigzag order before decoding and trimming. Both simulated SP+CP coverage and a real two-process Gloo CP=2 run passed.

Validation on DSW used a separate checkout with the exact changed source hashes. The focused suites passed 188 tests, TQ passed 8, and the tokenizer/fused-forward/MTP suites passed 185, for 381 passing CPU tests and no skips. A direct probe of the real vLLMHttpServer validated mapping/JSON-object handling. All pre-commit hooks passed. The legacy Megatron imports were also moved behind their version guard after this environment exposed the collection failure.

The new GPU reruns use the combined final review fixes from this PR, #7484 and #8032. Their results will be reported separately; the earlier synchronized-runtime measurements are not being presented as validation of those later changes.

Confirmed that the locked Bridge 0.6.2 wheel has no `glm5next` package. The GLM launcher now documents how to install the upstream Bridge revision that introduced `GLM53FlashModel` into each Ray node’s prepared environment, including its paired Megatron-Core. It shows the exact import check and uses `VERL_USE_UV=0` so the driver and workers keep that environment. [Original review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5760969042) · [Launcher setup](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/f9d15ef2735ec94646fe5725f8188cf00446e2fd/examples/tuning/lora/run_glm53_flash_megatron.sh#L12-L19)

On DSW, CPU-only imports of `GLM53FlashModel` and `KDALayerConfig` succeeded from the paired upstream sources (Bridge `58382ddf`, Core `902feb8e`) in an isolated directory. The existing DSW training environment separately imported the wrapper from Bridge `d16c26d5`. This commit changes launcher comments only. `bash -n examples/tuning/lora/run_glm53_flash_megatron.sh` and the relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

GPU integration validation completed on 4 × 8 H20s using a frozen combination of the reviewed production fixes from #7483, #7484 and #8032 (tree `c5015bdc45b2e606da73a291e39768d8055993be`). The later GLM dependency-comment and optimizer-group test follow-ups do not change the training implementation.

| Model/configuration | Nodes | Step-1 rollout/actor Pearson | Exit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GLM5.3 Flash BF16 | 2 | 0.999644935131073 | 0 |
| GLM5.3 Flash FP8 | 2 | 0.9987379908561707 | 0 |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 4 | 0.9988568425178528 | 0 |

These used batch/mini/n=2/2/4 and actual rollout decode logprobs, without teacher-forced logprob replacement or WOA overrides. Both GLM modes used FP8 KV cache. BF16 GLM used resync_base=True; FP8 GLM and DeepSeek used False. GLM gradient norms were nonzero (0.0870 and 0.1013). The small DeepSeek batch had identical rewards and zero gradient, so its result validates alignment rather than learning after a nonzero adapter update.

The tested dependency stack used Bridge source `d16c26d5`, GLM Core source `1ac85e91`, DeepSeek Core source `2dbc2cac`, and the installed vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev602+g0eb619dc5` wheel with the `1184b289` Python overlay and the native GLM packed-convolution LoRA loader correction. These results do not claim that the stock pinned Bridge wheel, arbitrary bare-BF16 GLM checkpoints, or the FSDP2 CUDA path were tested by these Megatron jobs.

The four-node Geo3k long run is now running with thinking=max, last20_novision, resync_base=False, batch64/mini64/n8 and a 400-step target. Convergence is still pending; starting that job is not being reported as a convergence result.

The GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint used by the launcher has root `model_type="glm5_next"`, architecture `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, text type `glm5_next_text`, and vision type `glm5_next_vision`. I checked the DSW checkpoint against the published configuration. The published GLM-5.3 text checkpoint uses `glm_moe_dsa` and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, so I’m keeping its existing text registration. [Original review](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5761250561) · [GLM-5.3-Flash config](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/blob/46a050bec13002ad29ee795c16e61cf4fa3c4a9c/config.json) · [GLM-5.3 text config](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3/blob/ba32f8c19c8738e2c57c71798c601d477a7bf844/config.json)

The agent loop reads the root config’s `model_type`. With `glm5_next` and its image processor, the resolver selects `VL_DEFAULT` and constructs the processor-backed `VLContinuousTokenBuilder`. Both DSW agent-loop logs (BF16 and FP8) reported `model_type='glm5_next'; falling back to vldefault` and completed rollout. The proposed registry change would target a different model family. [Agent-loop dispatch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/cd9330c25a9408aeedc87a5abfb88562e9318a05/verl/experimental/agent_loop/agent_loop.py#L537-L542) · [Registry](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/cd9330c25a9408aeedc87a5abfb88562e9318a05/verl/utils/tokenizer/continuous_token_wiring.py#L96-L103) · [Family resolution and construction](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/cd9330c25a9408aeedc87a5abfb88562e9318a05/verl/utils/tokenizer/continuous_token_wiring.py#L206-L279)

Additional CPU-only constructor validation: with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''` and the offline Hugging Face cache, the real `SingleTurnAgentLoop` constructed successfully using the actual GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint and selected `VLContinuousTokenBuilder`. Its multimodal check passed, and a real 112×112 image produced 34 prompt tokens, including 16 image tokens, plus `pixel_values` and `image_grid_thw`. The seven production files on this path match the tested runtime byte for byte. This directly exercises the constructor and prompt-processing path identified by the merge-risk summary; no new family registration is needed. The two-node BF16 and FP8 Geo3K runs also completed step 1 (Pearson 0.9996449351 and 0.9987379909).
